editorial: Imagine stepping into an old movie set where the only sound is the wind and the weight of unspoken longing. This film, Queer (2024), in its quiet setting in 1950s Mexico City, shapes a romantic drama that relies on subtlety rather than grand gestures. Joaquin Phoenix carries every scene with almost no dialogue, letting his nuanced gaze articulate decades of loneliness. You’ll find it compelling if you appreciate slow‑burn stories where the chemistry between two souls develops with quiet persistence. Some of the middle act feels a touch sluggish, making the pace feel uneven.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of quiet, character-driven cinema that explores love and loneliness amid history.
